title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Flavio Bolsonaro says he will ask courts to annul it. Serbia's Vučić also lost.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Monday, October 26, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 1 update on stories you're following and 7 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Lula wins Brazil's runoff as his rival refuses to concede
stories.why_important: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's runoff with 51.75% of the vote. Polls had predicted a tight race, but he secured a fourth term. His right-wing rival, Flavio Bolsonaro, refused to concede and said he would ask courts to cancel the result. How Brazil's institutions handle that challenge will shape Latin America's largest democracy.
stories.what_overlooked: Brazil's election court has already confirmed the result, so Bolsonaro's call to cancel it has no clear legal path. Lula's win also breaks a rightward trend across Latin America.
stories.prediction: Whether Bolsonaro's campaign files a case to cancel the result by midweek, and whether Brazil's armed forces publicly accept Lula's win.

stories.story_title: Serbia's Vučić concedes defeat to a student-led movement
stories.why_important: Vladimir Putin had endorsed Aleksandar Vučić, yet Serbia's dominant leader for over a decade conceded defeat in Sunday's snap parliament election. A student-led movement spent nearly two years protesting his government and will try to form a government instead.
stories.what_overlooked: Vučić left the presidency to run for prime minister, so this defeat ends his formal hold on power. The student coalition has never governed and has no agreed governing plan.
stories.prediction: Who the student movement picks as prime minister, and whether Vučić's party tries to block the handover in parliament.

stories.story_title: Venezuela's Machado returns home to a government that has not called elections
stories.why_important: María Corina Machado is Venezuela's opposition leader and a Nobel Prize winner. She returned home Sunday after ten months in exile and seven failed attempts. Tens of thousands greeted her convoy in Caracas, while acting president Delcy Rodríguez has stayed in office past her 90-day limit without calling elections.
stories.what_overlooked: Her failed return attempts had already hurt relations with the Trump administration, which backs Caracas's temporary government. Her arrival now tests whether Washington wants an election.
stories.prediction: Whether Venezuelan authorities allow Machado to hold public rallies this week, or move to detain or expel her.

quick_hits.text: Storms Boelo and Austen killed two men in Britain and cut power to more than 800,000 properties, with France and Germany also hit.
Ukraine's Zelensky said US, Ukrainian and Russian officials will meet in November, adding that territorial issues must be settled by leaders.
An Israeli strike on Gaza's Islamic University killed three security guards, part of ten students and educators killed in six days.
France's far-right leader Marine Le Pen launched her presidential campaign in Orléans, promising zero-tolerance policing as protests continued nationwide.
Flash floods inundated every district of Thailand's Phuket island, prompting evacuations and road closures as authorities warn of more rain.
A Russian inspector satellite made its closest approach yet to a Western spacecraft that supplies Ukraine with images, Meduza reported.
Netanyahu warned Iran and its proxies that any attempt to disrupt Tuesday's Israeli election would bring blows out of all proportion.
